Bin the cells of each path along pseudotime

Source: R/sc.squeeze.R
sc.squeeze.Rd

sc.squeeze() divides the pseudotime range of each path into bins of equal width and adds up the counts of the cells of each bin into pseudo-bulk counts. The number of bins of a path is that of a histogram rule (estBinSize()) times drop_fac, rounded up.

Each cell goes to the bin whose interval holds its pseudotime. As in Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.1, "bins are structured as left-closed and right-open intervals, except for the last bin, which is closed on both ends": a cell on the bound of two bins goes to the later one. The bounds are stored in the scmp_l_bound and scmp_u_bound columns of the bin metadata (cDense()).

The paths are binned, and their bins stored, in the order of the levels of the path column when it is a factor, and otherwise in the C-locale (byte) order of the labels, whatever the collation of the session. sc.set.poly() takes the first path as the reference unless told otherwise.

sc.squeeze(
  scmpObj,
  ptime_col = scmpObj@Parameters@ptime_col,
  path_col = scmpObj@Parameters@path_col,
  bin_method = "Sturges",
  drop_fac = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  bin_mem_col = "scmp_bin_members",
  bin_col = "scmp_bin",
  bin_size_col = "scmp_bin_size",
  bin_ptime_col = "scmp_binned_pseudotime",
  split_bins = FALSE,
  prune_bins = FALSE,
  assay_name = "counts",
  drop_trails = FALSE,
  aggregate = "sum",
  fill_gaps = FALSE,
  additional_params = list(use_unique_time_points = FALSE)
)

Arguments

scmpObj

A ScMaSigPro object.

ptime_col

The name of the column of the cell metadata that holds the pseudotime of each cell.

path_col

The name of the column of the cell or bin metadata that holds the path label of each cell or bin.

bin_method

The rule for the number of bins: "Sturges", "Sqrt", "Rice", "Doane", "Freedman.Diaconis" or "Scott.Normal" (see estBinSize()).

drop_fac

The drop factor of Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.1, at least 0.3: it multiplies the number of bins of the rule, and the product is rounded up. Values below 1 give fewer, wider bins.

verbose

Whether to print progress messages.

bin_mem_col

The name of the column of the bin metadata that holds the cells of each bin, separated by |.

bin_col

The name of the column of the bin metadata that holds the name of each bin.

bin_size_col

The name of the column of the bin metadata that holds the number of cells of each bin.

bin_ptime_col

The name of the column of the bin metadata that holds the binned pseudotime of each bin.

split_bins

Whether to divide the bins of a path that hold more cells than the mean plus the standard deviation of its bin sizes (see Details).

prune_bins

Whether to remove the bins of a path that hold fewer cells than the mean minus the standard deviation of its bin sizes (see Details).

assay_name

The name of the assay of the Sparse slot that holds the counts of the cells.

drop_trails

Whether to drop the last bins of the longer paths, so that every path has the binned pseudotime of the shortest.

aggregate

How the counts of the cells of a bin are combined: "sum" or "mean" (rounded to whole numbers).

fill_gaps

Whether to renumber the bins of a path whose binned pseudotime has gaps, such as after pruning.

additional_params

A list: use_unique_time_points = TRUE bins the distinct pseudotime values of each path instead of its cells.

Value

The object with the bins and their pseudo-bulk counts (bulk.counts) in the Dense slot and the binned pseudotime of each cell in the cell metadata.

Details

split_bins and prune_bins follow Section 2.2 of Srivastava et al. (2024): "scMaSigPro calculates the mean (\(\mu\)) and standard deviation (\(\sigma\)) of the sizes of all bins per path to establish maximum (\(\mu+\sigma\)) and minimum (\(\mu-\sigma\)) allowable bin sizes. Bins larger than the maximum size are divided, and those smaller than the minimum size can be optionally removed, ensuring uniform bin sizes. The process is repeated until all bins conform to the established size criteria." Both limits are set once, from the bins of the rule, empty bins included. A bin above the maximum is divided into the number of bins that the rule and drop_fac give for its cells, until no bin is larger; sc.squeeze() stops when a division gives back bins it has already made. A path with a single bin keeps it. Pruning comes after the divisions: a negative minimum removes no bin, and the cells of a removed bin stay in the Sparse slot without a bin.

References

Srivastava P, Benegas Coll M, Götz S, Nueda MJ, Conesa A (2024). scMaSigPro: differential expression analysis along single-cell trajectories. Bioinformatics 40(7), btae443. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae443

See also

estBinSize() for the rules that set the number of bins; plotBinTile() to see the bins.

Other workflow steps: sc.cluster.trend(), sc.filter(), sc.p.vector(), sc.restruct(), sc.set.poly(), sc.t.fit()

Examples

data("splat.sim", package = "scMaSigPro")
scmp <- as_scmp(splat.sim,
    additional_params = list(
        labels_exist = TRUE, exist_ptime_col = "Step",
        exist_path_col = "Group"
    ),
    verbose = FALSE
)
scmp <- sc.squeeze(scmp)
bins <- cDense(scmp)
head(bins[, c("Path", "scmp_binned_pseudotime", "scmp_bin_size")])
#>              Path scmp_binned_pseudotime scmp_bin_size
#> Path1_bin_1 Path1                      1            14
#> Path1_bin_2 Path1                      2            15
#> Path1_bin_3 Path1                      3             7
#> Path1_bin_4 Path1                      4            17
#> Path1_bin_5 Path1                      5            13
#> Path1_bin_6 Path1                      6            11
